records.stem: What is the mechanism of action of Tranexamic Acid

options.B: Competitive inhibition of plasminogen conversion to plasmin
options.D: Inhibition of vitamin K-dependent clotting factor synthesis
options.E: Activation of protein C by thrombomodulin

records.reason:
2 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Tranexamic acid is a lysine analogue that binds lysine-binding sites on plasminogen and plasmin, competitively inhibiting plasminogen activation to plasmin and thereby reducing fibrinolysis. Stoelting's Pharmacology & Physiology, p.653.

records.stem: PaCO2 response is unaffected by:
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Subanaesthetic concentrations of inhaled anaesthetics at 0.1 MAC do not alter the ventilatory response to carbon dioxide (Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, p.144). By contrast, the response is reduced during sleep and by increased work of breathing; hyperoxia removes the augmentation produced by peripheral chemoreceptors. Opioids cause dose-dependent depression of brainstem respiratory centres and alter both the slope and intercept of the ventilatory response to hypercarbia.

records.stem: Which artery is X pointing to in this diagram? [Figure: schematic of the arterial supply at the base of the brain (the circle of Willis and the vertebrobasilar system) viewed from below; X points to one of the two paired arteries that ascend and unite in the midline into a single artery giving off pontine branches.]
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

X indicates one of the paired vertebral arteries ascending towards the midline. The two vertebral arteries unite to form the single basilar artery, which then ascends on the pons and gives pontine branches. Thus, the basilar artery is the tempting alternative but lies distal to the union and is unpaired. These relationships are shown in Anatomy for Anaesthetists, p.263, Fig. 179, and Foundations of Anesthesia, p.241, Fig. 21.1.

records.stem: What is the most likely cause of the following arterial blood gas pH 7.43 PaO2 100 PaCO2 33 HCO3 21

options.D: A resident living on mount Everest
options.E: Patient having an acute panic attack

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

This is a compensated respiratory alkalosis: PaCO2 is reduced to 33 mm Hg, bicarbonate is reduced to 21 mmol/L by renal compensation, and pH is slightly alkaline. At term, progesterone increases ventilation, producing chronic respiratory alkalosis with renal bicarbonate loss; PaO2 remains normal. Vomiting causes metabolic alkalosis, whereas acetazolamide causes metabolic acidosis. Residence on Mount Everest causes hypoxaemia as well as respiratory alkalosis.

records.stem: An arterial blood gas obtained while breathing an FiO2 of 0.21 shows: pH 7.47, PaO2 60 mmHg, PaCO2 44 mmHg, and HCO3− 31 mmol/L. What is the primary acid–base disturbance?
records.reason:
1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

The corrected values show alkalemia with an increased bicarbonate concentration, identifying primary metabolic alkalosis. The PaCO2 is not reduced and is compatible with respiratory compensation. Normal bicarbonate is 22–26 mmol/L (Foundations of Anesthesia, p.687).

records.stem: What is the closest to cerebral O2 consumption at rest (mL/min)
records.reason:
Explanation written by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Resting cerebral oxygen consumption is approximately 3.5 mL O2·min−1·100 g−1. For a brain mass of about 1,400 g, total consumption is 3.5 × 14 = 49 mL O2·min−1, closest to 50 mL/min. Values near 3–5 mL/min describe consumption per 100 g of brain tissue, not whole-brain oxygen consumption.

records.stem: Water boiling at 100C has what SVP
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

A liquid boils when its saturated vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure. At the normal boiling point of water, 100°C, atmospheric pressure is 760 mm Hg; therefore, its saturated vapour pressure is 760 mm Hg. The value 47 mm Hg is the saturated vapour pressure of water at body temperature, not at 100°C. (Dorsch & Dorsch Equipment, p.89.)

records.stem: Where is inspiratory volatile anaesthetic concentration measured
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Inspiratory volatile anaesthetic concentration is measured from gas sampled close to the patient, typically at the sampling port of the HME, so it reflects the gas actually inspired. The common gas outlet is where the flowmeter gas mixture and vapour added by the vaporizer leave the anaesthetic machine and enter the breathing system; it therefore represents fresh-gas output rather than patient inspired concentration (Essentials of Anaesthetic Equipment, p.46).

records.stem: What is the oral bioavailability of Midazolam
records.reason:

Only about 50% of an orally administered dose of midazolam reaches the systemic circulation because of substantial first-pass hepatic metabolism. Its oral bioavailability therefore lies within 30–50% (Stoelting's Pharmacology & Physiology, p.187).

records.stem: What is the normal maternal uterine artery pCO2
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Normal pregnancy causes progesterone-mediated hyperventilation and a chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis. Maternal arterial PCO2 therefore falls from the non-pregnant value of approximately 40 mm Hg to approximately 32 mm Hg. Maternal uterine arterial blood has the same PCO2, making B correct.

records.stem: What is the cause of hyperkalaemia due to suxamethonium

options.D: General minor cell damage of whole body due to fasciculations

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Suxamethonium activates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, opening their ligand-gated cation channels. Sodium enters the muscle fibre while potassium exits down its concentration gradient, producing a net potassium loss from muscle and a rise in serum potassium. Upregulated peri- and extrajunctional receptors permit much greater potassium efflux and potentially life-threatening hyperkalaemia. Fasciculations themselves are not the mechanism. In healthy patients, the serum potassium increase is approximately 0.5 mEq L−1 (Evers, pp. 636, 639).

records.stem: What is true regarding the SVP of sevoflurane?

options.D: Increased to 259 mmHg with increased altitude

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

A liquid’s boiling point is the temperature at which its saturated vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure. Sevoflurane boils at 58.6°C at 760 mmHg; therefore, at approximately 58°C its saturated vapor pressure is approximately 760 mmHg. At 20°C it is 157 mmHg, compared with 238 mmHg for isoflurane. Saturated vapor pressure depends on agent and temperature, not altitude or ambient pressure (Dorsch & Dorsch Equipment, p.89).

records.stem: Which is true about Gabapentin

options.B: Causes GABA release/acts on GABAa receptors
options.C: Works on calcium channels in the CNS

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Gabapentin binds to the α2δ1 auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in the CNS. This reduces terminal depolarisation and excitatory neurotransmitter, particularly glutamate, release from primary afferents in the dorsal horn, producing antihyperalgesic effects. Despite being a GABA derivative, it does not act at GABAA receptors or affect GABAergic uptake or metabolism (Evers, p.581–582; Cousins & Bridenbaugh, p.781).

records.stem: What is false about Propofol and GABA-A interaction?
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

B is false. Activation of neuronal GABAA receptors opens chloride-selective channels, causing chloride influx down its concentration gradient in the mature brain. This hyperpolarizes, or prevents depolarization of, the postsynaptic membrane and reduces neuronal excitability. Propofol potentiates GABA-mediated channel opening at clinical concentrations and can directly activate GABAA currents at higher concentrations. It therefore does not cause chloride efflux under usual adult physiological conditions (Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, p.67; Evers, p.384).

records.stem: During anaesthetic, lack of heat generation is due to what is the most likely cause
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Skeletal muscle activity is a major source of thermogenesis. Shivering is involuntary skeletal muscle contraction; sustained shivering can double heat production. General anaesthesia reduces muscle tone and attenuates or abolishes shivering, particularly with neuromuscular blockade, thereby reducing heat generation. In contrast, peripheral vasodilation and reduced vasoconstriction primarily increase core-to-peripheral redistribution and environmental heat loss rather than directly reducing heat production (Foundations of Anesthesia, pp. 763–765).

records.stem: What line on the oxygen–haemoglobin dissociation curve below represents the umbilical vein in the placental circulation? [Figure: saturation against PO2 with three curves: a left-shifted curve, the standard adult curve and a right-shifted curve. A marks a point on the left-shifted curve at PO2 27 mmHg and 81% saturation; B marks a point lower on the left-shifted curve at PO2 16 mmHg and 40%; C marks the standard curve; D marks a point on the right-shifted curve at PO2 41 mmHg and 74%.]
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

The umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. Point A has a PO2 of 27 mmHg and saturation of 81%, consistent with umbilical venous blood on the left-shifted fetal haemoglobin curve. HbF has a P50 of 19 mmHg and greater oxygen affinity than HbA, facilitating oxygen transfer from maternal blood (Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, p.589). Point B represents less oxygenated fetal blood returning toward the placenta.

records.stem: Sudden increase in anatomical dead space in a ventilated anaesthetised patient. There is no change in the ventilated settings and an arterial blood gas is done 30 minutes later. What would be seen:
records.reason:
1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

At unchanged tidal volume and respiratory rate, increased anatomical dead space reduces alveolar ventilation. With constant CO2 production, PaCO2 therefore rises. End-tidal gas remains alveolar gas, so EtCO2 also rises toward the increased alveolar PCO2. Option B instead suggests an increased PaCO2–EtCO2 gradient, characteristic of increased alveolar rather than anatomical dead space (Stoelting, p.585).

records.stem: What condition is an absolute contraindication for angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Pregnancy is an absolute contraindication because ACE inhibitors are teratogenic and should not be used during pregnancy. Inhibition of the fetal renin–angiotensin system can impair fetal renal function and cause oligohydramnios. Rang & Dale’s Pharmacology, p.305, identifies teratogenesis as an adverse effect common to ACE inhibitors, and Evers, p.748, states explicitly that ACE inhibitors should not be used during pregnancy.

records.stem: What is the structure of sevoflurane
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Sevoflurane is a fluorinated methyl isopropyl ether: its ether oxygen links a one-carbon methyl group to a branched three-carbon isopropyl group. Therefore B correctly describes its parent ether structure. Methyl ethyl ether is incorrect; that carbon skeleton applies to agents such as desflurane, isoflurane and enflurane. (Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, pp.111, 113.)

records.stem: Which has the lowest oral bioavailability
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Naloxone has the lowest oral bioavailability, approximately 1–2%, because extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism leaves very little unchanged drug available systemically. Morphine is a tempting alternative, but its oral bioavailability is substantially higher at 20–40% (Evers, p.537). Oral bioavailability is determined by first-pass elimination between administration and entry into the systemic circulation.

records.stem: Which is true about Tapentadol

options.B: Has higher serotonin affect than tramadol
options.E: Is a racemic mixture of two enantiomers

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Tapentadol is extensively metabolised, predominantly by phase II glucuronidation, and its metabolites are pharmacologically inactive; therefore it has no active metabolites. CYP2D6 metabolism is only a minor pathway and does not generate an active metabolite. In contrast, tramadol undergoes CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation to O-desmethyltramadol, which has analgesic activity (Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, p.254).

records.stem: Which of these needs vitamin K for production
records.reason:
Explanation written and 2 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Protein S is a vitamin K-dependent anticoagulant protein produced in the liver. Reduced vitamin K is required for post-translational γ-carboxylation of glutamic acid residues, producing the functional Gla protein. Protein S acts as a cofactor that enhances activated protein C activity. Plasmin is generated from plasminogen in the fibrinolytic system, while thrombomodulin is an endothelial cell receptor for thrombin; neither requires vitamin K for production (Rang & Dale, pp. 328–329; Foundations of Anesthesia, p. 602).

records.stem: What changes occur in pregnancy at term:
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

At term, increased minute ventilation is produced predominantly by a larger tidal volume, with only a small rise in respiratory rate. Tidal volume increases by approximately 35–40% and respiratory rate by about 10%, increasing minute ventilation by about 50%. Progesterone stimulates the respiratory centres and shifts the ventilation–carbon dioxide response curve to the left (Kam & Power, p.483). Thus B best describes the ventilatory changes.

records.stem: What does Pancuronium cause
records.reason:
Explanation written by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Pancuronium causes tachycardia through a direct cardiac vagolytic effect: it blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors at clinically relevant doses. It may also enhance catecholamine release by blocking presynaptic muscarinic negative feedback and stimulating adrenergic nerve terminals. Bradycardia is therefore incorrect. As a steroidal neuromuscular blocker, pancuronium is not associated with histamine release at typical clinical doses. (Evers, p.630; Stoelting, p.346.)

records.stem: Which one of these is NOT a beta-lactam
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibacterial that targets bacterial DNA synthesis and structure, not a β-lactam. Meropenem is a carbapenem, ceftriaxone a cephalosporin, and amoxicillin a penicillin; all three are β-lactams. (Evers, pp. 966–968, 975.)

records.stem: What is NOT the most likely cause for a metabolic acidosis
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Albumin is a weak acid; reducing its concentration decreases the total weak-acid concentration and therefore has an alkalinising effect, rather than causing metabolic acidosis. By contrast, acute tubular necrosis may impair renal acid excretion, hyperchloraemia accompanies normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and free-water excess may cause dilutional acidosis. Hemmings & Hopkins, p.685, lists dilution and reduced acid secretion in acute renal failure as causes of metabolic acidosis.

records.stem: Neostigmine causes
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Neostigmine is a reversible carbamate anticholinesterase. It inhibits both acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, the latter being the principal cholinesterase in plasma; most peripherally acting anticholinesterases inhibit both enzymes approximately equally (Rang & Dale’s Pharmacology, p.198). Carbamylation of the catalytic site is reversed by hydrolysis over minutes. Increased acetylcholine causes muscarinic effects such as bradycardia, not tachycardia. As a quaternary amine, neostigmine does not cross the blood–brain barrier (Foundations of Anesthesia, pp.396, 438).

records.stem: Which of these can cross the blood–brain barrier? [Figure: four chemical structures. A: a phenyl ring with no ring hydroxyls carrying a CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH3 side chain. B: a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring carrying a CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH3 side chain. C: a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring carrying a CH2–CH2–NH2 side chain. D: a 3-hydroxyphenyl ring carrying a CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–NH2 side chain.]
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

A is ephedrine. Its lack of ring hydroxyl groups makes it less polar and more lipid soluble than B, C and D, allowing its uncharged fraction to diffuse across the blood–brain barrier. B and C have two phenolic hydroxyl groups, while D has one, increasing water solubility and limiting penetration. In general, passive blood–brain barrier penetration favours small non-polar molecules, whereas ionised species have very low lipid solubility (Rang & Dale, pp.124, 489).

records.stem: How much Na is normally reabsorbed by the kidney
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Normally, nearly all filtered sodium is reabsorbed. Stoelting’s Pharmacology & Physiology, p.433, gives a filtered load of 26,000 mEq/day, reabsorption of 25,850 mEq/day and 99.4% reabsorbed; thus 99% is the best answer. About 65% is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule alone, with further reabsorption along the loop of Henle, distal tubule and collecting duct. ADH primarily regulates distal nephron water reabsorption, so sodium reabsorption does not depend entirely on ADH.

records.stem: A pregnant woman at term is given a 1mg induction dose of Alfentanil. What percentage would be found IONISED in the foetus
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Alfentanil is a weak base with a pKa of approximately 6.5. Using the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation at normal fetal pH (approximately 7.3), about 14% is ionised, making 10% the closest option. The slightly lower fetal pH increases ionisation of weak bases, although the normal maternal–fetal pH difference is small (Evers, p.949). The 1 mg dose affects the amount present, not the percentage ionised.

records.stem: What is the goal MAP for a patient with raised ICP?
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) equals MAP minus the greater of ICP or CVP. In a patient with raised ICP, MAP must therefore be maintained at ICP + 60 mmHg to target a CPP of 60 mmHg, near the lower limit of cerebral autoregulation. A fixed MAP such as 100 mmHg may provide inadequate CPP when ICP is markedly elevated (Foundations of Anesthesia, p.245).

records.stem: Which law applies? Increasing airway pressure when a reservoir bag is squeezed
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Boyle’s law describes the inverse relationship between volume and absolute pressure for a fixed quantity of perfect gas at constant temperature: P1V1 = P2V2. Squeezing the reservoir bag decreases its volume, thereby increasing the pressure of the contained gas and the airway pressure (Nunn & Lumb’s Respiratory Physiology, p.529).

records.stem: This is a log dose-response curve for drug X (left curve) and drug Y (right curve). What is the potency of drug Y compared to drug X? [Figure: percentage of responders against log dose; both curves are sigmoid and reach 100%; the left curve (X) crosses 50% at a dose of 2 and the right curve (Y) at a dose of 16.]
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Both curves reach 100%, so compare the doses producing a response in 50% of the population. Drug X has an ED50 of 2 and drug Y an ED50 of 16. Because potency is the reciprocal of ED50, the potency of Y relative to X is (1/16)/(1/2) = 2/16 = 0.125. Thus Y is one-eighth as potent as X (Evers, p.31).

records.stem: In the patient shown sitting with the brain approximately 30 cm above the right atrium, what right-atrial MAP is required to provide a cerebral-level MAP of approximately 60 mmHg?
records.reason:
1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

A 30 cm elevation produces an approximately 22 mmHg hydrostatic pressure decrease (about 0.74 mmHg/cm). Thus, a right-atrial MAP of about 82 mmHg is required for a cerebral-level MAP of 60 mmHg; 80 mmHg is the closest option. Gravity decreases venous and arterial pressure above the heart (Stoelting, p.383). True CPP additionally subtracts the greater of ICP or CVP (Hemmings & Hopkins, p.245).

records.stem: In a healthy, drug-free adult, the illustrated EEG shows continuous, irregular, low-voltage, high-frequency (>13 Hz) asynchronous activity. Concurrent EOG shows no rapid eye movements, and EMG shows preserved muscle tone. What state does this most likely represent?
records.reason:
1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

High-frequency, low-voltage, irregular asynchronous activity is characteristic of alert wakefulness. REM can produce a very similar EEG, but absent rapid eye movements and preserved muscle tone exclude REM (Guyton & Hall, p.717; Kam & Power, p.92). The original key, sedated, cannot be inferred from this waveform. With the repaired stem, awake is the single best answer.

records.stem: Which of these is true about REM sleep

options.B: Is shorter earlier in the night cycles
options.E: Is associated with a synchronized, high-voltage EEG

records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

REM bouts last 5–30 minutes and are shortest when a person is very sleepy. As sleep progresses and the person becomes more rested, REM bouts increase in duration; therefore, REM sleep is shorter in the earlier night cycles. REM episodes consequently tend to lengthen towards morning (Guyton & Hall, p.713; Nunn & Lumb, p.234).

records.stem: What is the thermoneutral environmental temperature for a naked newborn/neonate
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

The thermoneutral temperature is the environmental temperature range in which body temperature is maintained with minimal oxygen consumption. For a naked, full-term newborn on the first day of life, this range is 32°C–34°C; therefore, 33°C is the best answer. Within this range, temperature is controlled by changes in skin blood flow alone. A temperature of 37°C approximates core temperature, not the thermoneutral environmental temperature (Kam & Power, p.498).

records.stem: Which of these is most likely true about the apex of the lung?
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

At the apex of the upright lung, perfusion decreases more than ventilation, producing a high ventilation-perfusion ratio. Consequently, alveolar gas approaches inspired gas: alveolar PO2 rises and alveolar PCO2 falls to approximately 28 mm Hg. Thus A is correct. West’s Respiratory Physiology, p.225, confirms that the apex has a high ventilation-perfusion ratio and reduced PCO2.

records.stem: 28-day old RBC's given via transfusion, bloods taken 1 hour post-transfusion would show p50 of?
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

After 28 days of storage, red-cell 2,3-DPG is negligible. One hour after transfusion, little restoration has occurred; transfused cells reach only about 50% of normal 2,3-DPG by 7 hours and baseline by 48 hours. Reduced 2,3-DPG increases haemoglobin–oxygen affinity, shifts the oxygen dissociation curve left and lowers P50 from its normal value of approximately 26 mm Hg. Thus 16 mm Hg is the best answer (Nunn & Lumb, p.180).

records.stem: What are the afferent and efferent nerves for gag reflex?
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

The afferent limb of the gag reflex is carried by the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX), which supplies sensation to the pharyngeal mucosa. The efferent limb is carried by the vagus nerve (X), whose pharyngeal branch supplies the pharyngeal muscles through the pharyngeal plexus (Anatomy for Anaesthetists, pp. 299, 306).

records.stem: On the following curve, what would explain a shift from point A to point B? [Figure: stroke volume against preload with two curves; point A lies on the lower curve and point B lies directly above it on the upper curve, at the same preload.]
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

Point B has a greater stroke volume at the same preload, indicating an upward shift of the ventricular function curve rather than movement along it. Increased contractility shifts this curve upward by increasing ventricular fibre shortening and ejection, thereby increasing stroke volume. Increased preload would instead move the operating point along the same Frank–Starling curve to a higher preload. Increased afterload shifts the ventricular function curve downward (Evers, p.334).

records.stem: Which coronary vessel is most likely to supply AV node
records.reason:
Explanation written and 1 distractor(s) added by the tracker's GPT generator (gpt-5.6-sol, prescribed-text grounded), 2026-09-08 — the key is unchanged and not examiner-verified.

The right coronary artery is most likely to supply the AV node, doing so in approximately 85% of people (Kam & Power, p.165). It gives rise to the AV nodal artery near the crux of the heart. In the minority with left-dominant circulation, supply may arise from the left circumflex artery, so the circumflex is a possible but less likely source.

records.stem: Which of the following does not cause inter-individual variation with response to heparin?

options.C: Zero order kinetics via saturation of heparinases

records.reason:
